cohort: Forty women who underwent post placental intrauterine contraceptive device insertion after Caesarean section.
finding: Post placental IUCD insertion was found to be an effective, safe, convenient, low-cost, and long-term method of post-partum contraception, with excessive vaginal bleeding as the most common complication and no cases of perforation or unintended pregnancy observed.
mod_finding: The study specifically recommends PPIUCD insertion for eligible post-partum women undergoing Caesarean section, noting a low perforation rate possibly due to the thick uterine wall post-delivery.
